one_liner: Squarespace Commerce REST APIs (orders, products, inventory, transactions, contacts, discounts, webhooks) with API keys (Commerce Advanced plan) or OAuth2 (registration form and review); an official vendor MCP server exists and includes commerce tools.
auth_notes: API keys are generated per site in Developer API Keys and never expire while the site is active. OAuth requires becoming a registered OAuth client via a request form; OAuth is the route for Extensions. Webhook subscriptions being OAuth-only comes from a third-party report, not the vendor pages.
access_notes: API-key path needs a paid Commerce Advanced site. Multi-user OAuth needs a registration request to Squarespace. No free path is evidenced in the pages.
blocker_notes: Multi-user OAuth requires applying to become a registered OAuth client. API-key testing needs a paid Commerce Advanced plan. The earlier claim that the official MCP covers only domains is contradicted by the vendor's help page, which mentions commerce tools.

evidence.quote: Depending on your development needs, you can use a generated API key or start the OAuth process with Squarespace to become a registered OAuth client.
A Squarespace merchant site can use both API keys and OAuth for data access, but Squarespace Extensions are required to use OAuth.
**Orders**, **Inventory**, and **Transactions** are only available in the Commerce Advanced plan.
With [Squarespace's Commerce Advanced](https://www.squarespace.com/pricing) plan, you can develop a custom application for a Squarespace merchant site.
All Commerce APIs are built on HTTPS and designed with REST principles in mind.
**Webhook Subscriptions API:** Subscribe to notifications from a site, like when an order was created, by configuring a webhook endpoint.
The Squarespace MCP server connects AI assistants, like Claude and ChatGPT, to Squarespace tools using Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Tools are organized by product area, like domains and commerce, and we add new tools over time.
